A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VALUEFLOW research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–J are available and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original embedding evaluations, ten-model steering experiments, OpinionQA results, and human evaluation, with additional empirical analyses throughout the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds hierarchical-composition results in Table 13, alongside revised OpinionQA results and additional statistical reporting.

M1.justification: The documented HIVES architecture, two-stage objectives, VIDB construction, Plackett–Luce evaluator, and steering procedures remain unchanged. Hierarchical composition tests existing multi-value prompting; expanded explanations do not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: v2 adds hierarchical steering on ValueNet queries, including finer-grained constituent targets such as Caring and Dependability (Table 13). This extends steering-task coverage; the existing training corpora, demographic populations, multilingual evaluations, and Buddhist-ethics setting remain.

E2.justification: New Table 13 introduces an explicit comparison between constituent-based steering and direct target-value steering. This is a limited within-framework comparison addition; established baselines, including UniVar, base Qwen3 embeddings, default demographic prompts, and Modular Pluralism, remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds direct-versus-constituent steering comparisons under positive and negative targets and reports demographic-alignment testing across decoding temperatures from 0.0 to 0.8. The existing 500-prompt evaluation, 5% profiling split, and ranking-window settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 7.1 and Table 13 add a focused test of whether constituent values induce their associated target value. Section 6.3 newly reports temperature robustness. Existing ranking ablations, refusal analyses, context tests, and multi-turn analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 6.3 newly reports paired t-tests for OpinionQA gains, with t approximately 16–20 and p below 10^-60. No increased run count or new seed information is specified; the 50 repetitions documented for multi-turn experiments already appeared in v1.

E6.justification: OpinionQA Table 2 becomes Table 3 with revised scores and single Profile rows replacing separate Duty/SVT rows. Phi-4's default average changes from 53.2 to 51.2; its earlier SVT religion score of 58.9 is replaced by a Profile score of 57.4. These profile rows are not established as equivalent settings. Table 13 adds composition results, while most existing numerical evidence is retained.

T1.justification: The steerability definition, hierarchical and anchor objectives, Plackett–Luce equations, calibration derivations, and Appendix D.9 justification are retained. Expanded notation explanations introduce no new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain unified value extraction, intensity evaluation and steering, asymmetric controllability, multi-value composition, and improved demographic alignment. Although the abstract drops 'first,' the priority claim remains in Sections 2 and 8; the revised Phi-4 example preserves the claimed greater-than-ten-point improvement.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies intensities as value-conditional rather than globally comparable and discusses overlapping macro-values, scalar representation, evaluation overhead, and independent component use. It also replaces four steerability regimes with three and interprets the new composition results as broadly matching direct steering.

D1.justification: Table 3 newly identifies its average as a micro-average over examples, but removes the Duty/SVT profile identifiers, reducing configuration traceability. Training hyperparameters, algorithms, and licensing details remain unchanged. The main-text disclosure of pairwise VIDB construction was already documented in v1's appendix.

R1.justification: The cited research and substantive positioning are retained. Changes such as Rozen et al.'s year moving from 2024 to 2025 and edited reference metadata concern the same works, not additions to related research.

P1.justification: v2 expands explanations in Sections 4–6, rewrites the model-group summary and conclusion, and adds Impact Statement and Acknowledgments sections. It also updates affiliations and publication text, corrects cross-references, and revises the LLM-use disclosure. The overall organization and most appendix prose remain.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 6 have revised axes, ordering, and markers; Figure 4's caption correctly distinguishes absolute intensities from shifts. v2 adds illustrative dataset Table 2 and composition Table 13, restructures the OpinionQA table, and reformats existing diagrams. Corresponding appendix figures are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: Explicitly limiting cross-value score interpretation and correcting Figure 4's caption reduce potential misreading, while Table 13 adds useful composition evidence. These gains are tempered by the unexplained replacement of theory-specific OpinionQA profiles and sparse documentation of the new temperature and significance checks.
